_note: Two panes, each holding several panels as tabs. Click a tab to switch to it, or drag one out to give it a pane of its own.

- Switch between the tabs in each pane.
- Drag the Status tab out and drop it on the right edge of the window, so it gets its own column.
- Drag it back onto the middle of the Packets pane, to stack it there again.
- Drag a tab along its own tab row to reorder the tabs.

**Moving a panel:** press its title bar - the empty space, the title, or a tab - and drag. The panel leaves the layout and a chip with its name follows the mouse; a see-through rectangle shows where it'll land.

- **The middle of a pane:** the panel joins it as a tab.
- **Near one of a pane's edges:** the pane splits, and the panel takes that half.
- **A tab row:** the panel goes in as a tab, right where the marker is.
- **The very edge of a group of panes:** a thin band along it docks the panel beside the whole group - near the window's edges, beside everything.
- **Anywhere else, or Esc:** the panel goes back where it was.

**Minimizing:** the bar at the left of a title bar minimizes that pane to just its title, giving its room to the panes beside it; the square it turns into brings it back to its size. Minimize every pane in a column (or row) and the whole column lays flat the other way, its titles turned sideways.
Your layout is saved with the workspace, like your inputs. **Reset Layout** (under **Edit Workspace**) puts every panel back where it started.
_dev_note: A demo of docking (see widgets/frame_widgets/docking.py) - no lesson, just a layout to rearrange.
